findings.title: Duplicate method definition `downsize` silently overrides original signature
findings.body: Two `self.downsize` methods are defined (lines 145 and 149), the second overriding the first. Any caller using the old 4-arg signature `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` (e.g. existing callers elsewhere in the codebase) will now get wrong behavior since `max_height` is silently dropped and `opts` is misassigned, or will raise ArgumentError due to mismatched arity. This is a backward-incompatible API break hidden behind a redefinition rather than an explicit rename/removal.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failure and risks corrupting original upload file
findings.body: The while loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` in-place up to 5 times without checking the boolean return value of `downsize`/`convert_with`. If the conversion fails (returns false), the loop still decrements `attempt` and continues, and `tempfile.size` is reread assuming the file was modified; on failure the original tempfile could be left in a bad/truncated state (since `to` == `from`, a failed convert may truncate the destination file) and the subsequent `Upload.create_for` would ingest a corrupted file without any error being surfaced to the user.

findings.title: download size cap decoupled from max_image_size_kb, now hardcoded then downsized after full download
findings.body: Previously `FileHelper.download` capped the download at `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`; now it's hardcoded to `10.megabytes`. For non-image attachments this silently increases the max download size regardless of site configuration, and for images the full (now up to 10MB) file is downloaded before any downsizing attempt, increasing bandwidth/memory usage compared to before even though the final image size enforcement still happens via the new downsize loop. This changes documented/configured size limit behavior without being mentioned in the PR description.

findings.title: Hardcoded max upload size removes site-setting-based validation
findings.body: `maxSizeKB` is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` instead of reading `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (and similarly `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` at line 246). This breaks the ability for admins to configure max upload size per type via site settings; client-side validation will always allow uploads up to 10MB regardless of the actual configured `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb`, which could mismatch the server-side limits and confuse users with incorrect error messages or allow oversized uploads to be attempted unnecessarily.
